posts.text:
Dominica can require a 3-year property hold; Saint Kitts and Nevis requires 7.

Compare five Caribbean citizenship routes by family contribution and asset rules. USD base amounts exclude fees; approval checks apply.
posts.alt: Dominica flag beside a property-holding comparison. Dominica: 3 years from citizenship, or 5 years before resale to another citizenship-by-investment applicant. Saint Kitts and Nevis: approved developer property requires a minimum 7-year hold. Qualifying family and asset conditions differ; fees are extra and approval checks apply.

posts.text:
Dominica EDF: USD 200,000 alone or USD 250,000 for applicant + 3 qualifying dependants.

Approved property starts at USD 200,000; hold 3 years from citizenship, or 5 before resale to another CBI applicant.
posts.alt: Dominica flag and two citizenship routes. EDF: USD 200,000 single applicant or USD 250,000 with up to 3 qualifying dependants. Approved property: from USD 200,000 plus USD 75,000 main-applicant government fee. Hold 3 years from citizenship, or 5 before resale to another CBI applicant. Other fees and approval checks apply.

posts.text:
Antigua and Barbuda: USD 230,000 NDF covers a family of up to 4, plus fees.

Approved property starts at USD 300,000, held for 5 years after purchase unless replaced with another officially approved property.
posts.alt: Antigua and Barbuda flag and two citizenship routes. NDF: USD 230,000 for up to 4 qualifying family members plus USD 20,000 processing. Approved property: from USD 300,000, held 5 years from purchase unless replaced with another officially approved property. Larger NDF families retain the USD 230,000 base with incremental processing fees. Other fees and approval checks apply.

posts.text:
Grenada: USD 235,000 NTF for up to 4 people; siblings and parents/grandparents 55 or younger cost extra.

Qualifying tourism shares start at USD 270,000 plus USD 50,000; 5 years before resale to another CBI applicant.
posts.alt: Grenada flag and citizenship routes. NTF: USD 235,000 for up to 4 qualifying family members; siblings and parents or grandparents aged 55 or under cost extra. Tourism share: USD 270,000 plus USD 50,000 government contribution; approved units, 2 or more joint buyers and developer equity conditions. Resale to another CBI applicant requires 5 years from citizenship. General approved-project threshold: USD 350,000. Other fees and approval checks apply.

posts.text:
Saint Kitts and Nevis: USD 250,000 SISC covers one applicant or family up to 4. Extra dependants: USD 25,000 under 18; USD 50,000 at 18+.

Approved developer property starts at USD 325,000 with a 7-year hold.
posts.alt: Saint Kitts and Nevis flag and citizenship routes. SISC: USD 250,000 for one applicant or up to 4 qualifying family members. Extra dependants: USD 25,000 under 18 or USD 50,000 at 18+. Approved developer property: from USD 325,000, minimum 7-year hold, plus USD 25,000 main-applicant post-approval fee. Due diligence and purchase costs are extra; approval checks apply.

posts.text:
Saint Lucia: USD 240,000 NEF for applicant + up to 3 qualifying dependants.

Alternative: USD 300,000 National Action Bonds held 5 years without interest, plus USD 50,000 administration; other fees extra.

posts.alt: Saint Lucia flag and citizenship routes. NEF: USD 240,000 for applicant plus up to 3 qualifying dependants.
